mainTopic: How ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן explain the dispute between the רבנן and רבי שמעון about an oath not to eat followed by eating נבילות, and how forbidden food can count as 'eating' for an oath.
overview: The משנה taught that if a person swore 'I will not eat' and then ate נבילות, the רבנן say he is liable and רבי שמעון exempts him. ריש לקיש explains that the oath was about less than a כזית. רבי יוחנן explains that the oath covered permitted food too, so it is an איסור כולל. The amud opens with ריש לקיש's point that איסור כולל only works for prohibitions that come on their own, not for an oath a person takes on himself. The גמרא then shows how each one explains רבי שמעון. For ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון holds that even a tiny amount is already forbidden by the Torah. For רבי יוחנן, רבי שמעון rejects איסור כולל, as seen from his ruling about eating נבילה on יום הכפורים. Next the גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with the rule of לאו והן: how could his oath exist in the positive form? It answers, following רבא, that the oath was a general 'I will not eat', and real food, even forbidden food, counts as eating, while dirt does not. רב מרי brings support from a משנה about a קונם vow. The גמרא begins to reject that proof, and the argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש limits the inclusive-prohibition rule
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains why he does not accept רבי יוחנן's approach. The rule of איסור כולל only works for a prohibition that comes by itself, like יום הכפורים. It does not work for a prohibition a person creates himself, like a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We only say איסור כולל] with a prohibition that comes on its own. With a prohibition a person brings on himself, we do not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes ריש לקיש's answer to the question of why he did not explain the משנה the way רבי יוחנן did. He says the 'inclusive prohibition' rule does not apply to oaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one prohibition cannot take hold on something already forbidden. An 'inclusive' prohibition, which also covers permitted things, is an exception. ריש לקיש says this exception only works for prohibitions that come automatically, like the fast of יום הכפורים. A שבועה is a prohibition the person makes himself, so it cannot take hold on food the Torah already forbids, such as נבילות.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'inclusive prohibition': a new prohibition that covers both already-forbidden and permitted things, which can then take hold even on the forbidden ones
A prohibition that comes on its own, set by the Torah or by time (like יום הכפורים)
A prohibition a person creates himself, such as a vow or an oath
We do not say (the rule does not apply)

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence that began on the previous page. It is the end of ריש לקיש's answer, not a brand-new statement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the basic split. רבי יוחנן lets a שבועה take hold on forbidden food through איסור כולל, and ריש לקיש does not. That split drives the rest of the section.

phrases.english: [only] with a prohibition that comes on its own;
phrases.notes: The sentence began on the previous page: 'When do we say איסור כולל? Only...' Think of יום הכפורים, which forbids food automatically.

phrases.english: but with a prohibition that comes through the person himself,
phrases.notes: He means a שבועה or a נדר, which the person takes on by his own words.

phrases.english: we do not say [that rule].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's answer to a question asked on the previous page: why didn't he explain the משנה like רבי יוחנן?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: איסור כולל only applies to automatic prohibitions, not to self-imposed ones like oaths.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason according to רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: According to ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון's exemption is easy to explain. רבי שמעון holds that even a tiny amount of forbidden food is already forbidden by the Torah, so the oath has nothing to add. According to רבי יוחנן, why would רבי שמעון exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to ריש לקיש, this is why רבי שמעון exempts. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, any amount at all counts for lashes, and the כזית measure was only given for a קרבן. But according to רבי יוחנן, what is רבי שמעון's reason for exempting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that ריש לקיש's explanation fits רבי שמעון well, backed by a ברייתא. It then asks how רבי יוחנן would explain רבי שמעון's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's case is an oath about less than a כזית. רבי שמעון holds that even a tiny amount of forbidden food is forbidden and can bring מלקות, so the person is already 'sworn from Sinai' on it and the new oath cannot take hold. That neatly explains why רבי שמעון exempts. רבי יוחנן's case is an oath on a full amount that includes permitted food, so this reason does not help him, and the גמרא asks what reason he would give.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it works out fine (sets up a contrast: 'but according to the other view...')
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit
Lashes (מלקות), the punishment for breaking a negative commandment
An olive-bulk, the standard minimum amount for eating
An offering brought for an accidental sin
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Granted, according to Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָא פָטַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן;
phrases.english: it is because of this that Rabbi Shimon exempts;
phrases.notes: 'This' means even a tiny amount is already forbidden by the Torah, so an oath about less than a כזית has nothing to take hold on.

phrases.english: as it was taught [in a ברייתא]: Rabbi Shimon says:
Any amount at all [is enough] for lashes,
and they only said an olive-bulk for an offering.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan,
what is the reason of Rabbi Shimon, who exempts?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָא פָטַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having laid out the two approaches, the גמרא now tests how each one explains רבי שמעון's side of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי שמעון's reason for exempting, according to רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה?
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש has a ready reason for רבי שמעון from a ברייתא, while רבי יוחנן seems to have none.

steps.title: רבי שמעון rejects inclusive prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן's whole reason for liability, according to רבי יוחנן, is איסור כולל. רבי שמעון simply follows his usual view that איסור כולל does not take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the reason [of the רבנן] anything other than איסור כולל? רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, since he does not accept איסור כולל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן. רבי שמעון exempts because he does not accept the 'inclusive prohibition' rule at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the רבנן make the person liable only because his oath covered permitted food too, which makes it an איסור כולל. רבי שמעון generally holds that an inclusive prohibition cannot take hold where a prohibition already exists. So the oath does not take hold on the נבילות, and he exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: Is the reason anything other than...? (a rhetorical way of saying 'the only reason is...')
Following his own reasoning (consistent with what he says elsewhere)
He does not hold of / does not accept

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי הוּא טַעְמָא – אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל;
phrases.english: Is the reason [of the רבנן] anything other than because of an inclusive prohibition?
Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
that he does not hold of an inclusive prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי הוּא טַעְמָא – אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 on behalf of רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tie the dispute to a known general position (רבי שמעון לטעמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן had no way to explain רבי שמעון's exemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון rejects איסור כולל in general, so according to רבי יוחנן the oath never takes hold on the נבילות.

steps.title: Proof: eating נבילה on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves that רבי שמעון rejects איסור כולל. He says someone who eats נבילה on יום הכפורים is exempt from the יום הכפורים penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, one who eats נבילה on יום הכפורים is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that רבי שמעון really holds there is no איסור כולל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fast of יום הכפורים forbids all food, so it is an inclusive prohibition. Still, רבי שמעון says it does not take hold on נבילה, which was already forbidden, and the person is exempt for eating on יום הכפורים. This shows his general rule, and it supports the answer in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an animal that died without proper שחיטה, forbidden to eat
The Day of Atonement, when eating is forbidden
Exempt (here, from the penalty for eating on יום הכפורים)

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון exempts because even a tiny amount is already forbidden by the Torah. According to רבי יוחנן, he exempts because he rejects איסור כולל (see נבילה on יום הכפורים).

phrases.english: As it was taught [in a ברייתא]: Rabbi Shimon says:
One who eats non-kosher meat on Yom Kippur is exempt.
phrases.notes: He means exempt from the יום הכפורים penalty, because the fast's prohibition cannot take hold on meat that is already forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הָאוֹכֵל נְבֵילָה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 3 that רבי שמעון rejects איסור כולל.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון does not accept איסור כולל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון exempts one who eats נבילה on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: How can רבי יוחנן's oath work in the positive?
steps.stepSummary: A שבועת ביטוי only brings a קרבן if it can be said both ways, 'I will' and 'I will not' (לאו והן). ריש לקיש's case works both ways. In רבי יוחנן's case the negative works, but how could a positive oath to eat נבילות ever take hold?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to ריש לקיש, you can find it both as a 'no' and as a 'yes.' But according to רבי יוחנן: granted, you can find a 'no,' but how can you find a 'yes'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. His kind of oath only seems to work in the negative ('I won't eat'), but an oath that brings a קרבן must also work in the positive ('I will eat').
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on the פסוק 'להרע או להיטיב,' a שבועה only brings a קרבן if the same kind of oath could also be made the other way. For ריש לקיש, a person can swear to eat a tiny amount or swear not to eat it, so both ways work for the רבנן. For רבי יוחנן, 'I won't eat נבילות and permitted food' takes hold through איסור כולל, but an oath to eat נבילות cannot take hold against the Torah. So where is the positive version? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No' and 'yes': an oath must be possible both negatively ('I won't') and positively ('I will')
You can find it (a real case where it applies)
How?

steps.confusionAlert: 'לאו והן' is not about this specific person's oath. It asks whether this TYPE of oath could also exist in the opposite form. If it can't, it is not the kind of שבועה that brings a קרבן.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Reish Lakish,
you find it with 'no' and 'yes';
phrases.notes: An oath on a spoken statement only brings a קרבן if it can go both ways, 'I will' or 'I won't.' ויקרא 5:4.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yochanan,
granted, a 'no' — you can find it,
but a 'yes' — how can you find it?
phrases.notes: An oath to eat נבילות can't take hold, since the Torah already forbids them. So the positive side seems impossible.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּלָאו וָהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי שמעון to a new challenge against רבי יוחנן's explanation of the רבנן, based on the לאו והן requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation that the משנה deals with an inclusive oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שבועה that brings a קרבן must be possible in both negative and positive forms. רבי יוחנן's case seems to exist only in the negative, since a positive oath to eat נבילות cannot take hold.

steps.title: The oath was a general 'I will not eat,' like רבא's case of dirt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the oath did not mention נבילות at all. It was a plain 'I will not eat.' Just as eating dirt does not break such an oath, because dirt is not food, eating forbidden meat does break it, because it is real food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like רבא's ruling. רבא said: if someone says 'I swear I will not eat' and then eats dirt, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. It says the oath was a general 'I will not eat,' not an oath about נבילות specifically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A general oath like 'I will eat' or 'I will not eat' clearly works both ways, so the rule of לאו והן is satisfied. The only question is what counts as 'eating.' רבא teaches that dirt is not eating, which implies that real food, even forbidden food like נבילות, is eating and is covered by the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a sign that the גמרא is giving a new explanation
Like רבא, following his ruling
An oath that I will not eat
Dirt, something that is not food
Exempt, he owes nothing

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that the oath fails. He is saying that eating dirt does not count as 'eating,' so the oath was never broken.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fixes the problem of לאו והן for רבי יוחנן. A general oath works both ways, and the איסור כולל lets it take hold on נבילות as part of all foods.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like Rava,
as Rava said:
"An oath that I will not eat,"
and he ate dirt, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 about לאו והן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the oath was general, not specific to נבילות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath was 'I will eat נבילות,' which cannot take hold in the positive
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath was a general 'I will not eat.' Real food, even forbidden food, counts as eating, while dirt does not

steps.title: רב מרי brings support that eating forbidden food counts as eating
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says a משנה already teaches this. A man made a קונם vow forbidding his wife to benefit from him if he had eaten today. He had eaten נבילות and other forbidden creatures, and his wife becomes forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: We also learned this in a משנה. If a man says, 'It is קונם for my wife to benefit from me if I ate today,' and he had eaten נבילות, טריפות, שקצים or רמשים, his wife is forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי brings a proof from a משנה that eating forbidden food is called 'eating.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man said 'if I ate today,' and the only thing he ate was forbidden food. Since the vow takes effect and his wife becomes forbidden, the משנה treats his eating of forbidden food as real eating. This supports the idea from step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this, a sign that a proof is coming
A word used to make something forbidden, like a vow
Animals with a deadly injury, which are forbidden to eat
Disgusting creatures and creeping things, which are forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Rav Mari said,
we too have learned this:
"It is konam for my wife to benefit from me
if I ate today,"
and he had eaten neveilos and treifos,
repugnant creatures and creeping things,
his wife is forbidden to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for step 6's idea that forbidden food counts as eating
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a קונם vow: 'my wife is forbidden to benefit from me if I ate today'

steps.title: The גמרא starts to push away רב מרי's proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the two cases can be compared. In the קונם case, he ate first and only afterward made his statement about it. The explanation of why that matters continues after this line.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, since he first ate the food and only afterward swore about it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to reject רב מרי's proof. This line only sets up the difference, and the rest of the argument comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the קונם case, the eating had already happened before he spoke, so his words 'if I ate' describe what he actually did, forbidden food included. In our case, he swears about eating that has not happened yet. The גמרא is pointing to this difference in order, and the rest of its explanation continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? A sign that a proof is being rejected
At first, from the beginning
And afterward he swore

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, since at first he ate it
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets, and the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. The same is true in the next row.

phrases.english: and only afterward swore about it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב מרי's proof only. The idea of step 6 is not rejected here
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the קונם case the eating came before the statement, so he was describing eating that had already happened. In our case the oath is about future eating. The full explanation continues on the next amud
